posts.title: Temporary trade-liberalisation measures applicable to Armenian products
posts.label: ✅ Adopted — Council gave the final green light
posts.summary: This law removes temporary trade barriers on products from Armenia, making it easier and cheaper for Armenian goods to be imported and sold.
posts.whatsNext: Signature by the Parliament and Council presidents, then publication in the Official Journal. It enters into force on the date the act sets — by default the 20th day after publication.

posts.title: Establishing the Union Customs Code and the European Union Customs Authority
posts.label: 📜 Published in the Official Journal
posts.summary: The law establishes a unified customs code for trade across the EU and creates a new authority to manage and enforce customs rules. This sets out how goods are classified, taxed, and processed when crossing EU borders.
posts.whatsNext: It's law. It enters into force on the date it specifies or, if none, the 20th day after publication in the Official Journal.

posts.title: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1139 as regards simplification and the transposition of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
posts.label: 📋 New legislative proposal
posts.summary: This proposal seeks to simplify rules governing fishing subsidies and align them with international agreements on reducing harmful fishing practices. It aims to make it easier for countries to follow these rules while ensuring compliance with global trade standards on fisheries support.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament's lead committee and the Council's working party examine it in parallel. No deadline applies at this stage; most files take one to two-plus years.

posts.title: Instrument for Nuclear Safety Cooperation 2028–2034
posts.label: 🗳️ Parliament adopted its opinion (consultation)
posts.summary: This instrument would provide funding and a framework for cooperation among countries on nuclear safety matters over the period 2028–2034. It aims to support activities related to maintaining safe nuclear operations and managing nuclear-related risks across participating nations.
posts.whatsNext: Now in the Council's hands: it can adopt the act (usually by unanimity), amend it, or park it indefinitely — consultation sets no deadline.

posts.title: Establishing the Single Market and Customs Programme for the period 2028-2034
posts.label: ↩️ Plenary sent the file back to committee
posts.summary: This proposal aims to set up a new funding and coordination programme to support the smooth operation of Europe's internal market and customs systems over the coming years. The programme would help ensure that goods, services, and people can move freely across European borders while maintaining proper customs checks and safety standards.
posts.whatsNext: The committee will keep working on the text — typically to continue negotiations — before it returns to plenary. No deadline applies.

posts.title: Establishing the Union Customs Code and the European Union Customs Authority
posts.label: ✅ Act adopted — Parliament approved the Council's position
posts.summary: The law establishes a unified customs code for trade across the EU and creates a new authority to manage and enforce customs rules. This sets out how goods are classified, taxed, and processed when crossing EU borders.
posts.whatsNext: Adopted in the wording of the Council's first-reading position. Signature by the Parliament and Council presidents follows, then publication in the Official Journal and entry into force on the date the act sets.

posts.title: Market stability reserve for the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS): ceasing the invalidation of allowances
posts.label: ↩️ Plenary sent the file back to committee
posts.summary: The proposal aims to stop the automatic cancellation of emissions allowances under the EU's carbon trading scheme. This would allow more allowances to remain in circulation within the market stability reserve system.
posts.whatsNext: The committee will keep working on the text — typically to continue negotiations — before it returns to plenary. No deadline applies.

posts.title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: extension of its scope to downstream goods and anti-circumvention measures
posts.label: ↩️ Plenary sent the file back to committee
posts.summary: The proposal aims to expand a carbon pricing system at the border to cover products made from materials that have already been subject to carbon charges, preventing companies from avoiding the rules by shifting production stages. It also seeks to introduce measures to stop businesses from circumventing the system through indirect routes or loopholes.
posts.whatsNext: The committee will keep working on the text — typically to continue negotiations — before it returns to plenary. No deadline applies.

posts.title: Establishing the Temporary Decarbonisation Fund
posts.label: ↩️ Plenary sent the file back to committee
posts.summary: This proposal aims to create a temporary financial fund designed to support efforts to reduce carbon emissions and transition toward cleaner energy sources. The fund would seek to provide financial resources to help achieve environmental and climate goals.
posts.whatsNext: The committee will keep working on the text — typically to continue negotiations — before it returns to plenary. No deadline applies.

posts.summary: The law establishes a unified customs code for trade across the EU and creates a new authority to manage and enforce customs rules. This sets out how goods are classified, taxed, and processed when crossing EU borders.
posts.whatsNext: Council formal adoption is next, often without debate.

posts.label: 🧭 Negotiating mandate for trilogue talks
posts.summary: The proposal aims to stop the automatic cancellation of emissions allowances under the EU's carbon trading scheme. This would allow more allowances to remain in circulation within the market stability reserve system.
posts.whatsNext: Trilogue talks with the Council can begin once the Council side has its own mandate. Closed-door rounds follow; timing is not published.

posts.title: Establishing the Union Customs Code and the European Union Customs Authority
posts.label: ✍️ Signed by the European Parliament and the Council
posts.summary: The law establishes a unified customs code for trade across the EU and creates a new authority to manage and enforce customs rules. This sets out how goods are classified, taxed, and processed when crossing EU borders.
posts.whatsNext: Publication in the Official Journal is next; the act enters into force on the date it specifies (default: the 20th day after publication).

posts.title: Air passenger rights
posts.label: ✍️ Signed by the European Parliament and the Council
posts.summary: This law establishes protections and compensation rights for airline passengers, including provisions for assistance during delays and cancellations. It requires airlines to inform passengers of their rights and provide care such as meals and accommodation when necessary. Passengers can claim compensation from airlines for significant delays or cancellations under certain circumstances.
posts.whatsNext: Publication in the Official Journal is next; the act enters into force on the date it specifies (default: the 20th day after publication).

posts.title: Amending certain production, labelling and certification rules and certain rules on trade with third countries
posts.label: 🧭 Negotiating mandate for trilogue talks
posts.summary: This proposal aims to update the rules for how certain products are made, labeled, and certified, as well as how they can be bought and sold with countries outside the EU. The changes would modernize these existing regulations to reflect current needs.
posts.whatsNext: Trilogue talks with the Council can begin once the Council side has its own mandate. Closed-door rounds follow; timing is not published.

posts.title: Trans-European energy infrastructure: guidelines
posts.label: 🧭 Negotiating mandate for trilogue talks
posts.summary: This proposal aims to establish guidelines for energy infrastructure projects across Europe to improve connectivity and energy supply between member states. It seeks to coordinate the planning and development of major energy networks, such as pipelines and electricity lines, to strengthen Europe's energy security and integration.
posts.whatsNext: Trilogue talks with the Council can begin once the Council side has its own mandate. Closed-door rounds follow; timing is not published.

posts.title: EU Emissions Trading System: heat and fuel benchmark values for 2026–2030
posts.label: 🗳️ Parliament adopted its 1st-reading position
posts.summary: This proposal aims to update the standard reference values used to measure heat and fuel efficiency under the EU's emissions trading system for the years 2026 to 2030. The revised benchmarks would establish new targets for how much heat and fuel different industries should use compared to the best performers in their sector.
posts.whatsNext: The Council decides: accept Parliament's text as-is (the act is then adopted) or adopt its own position — for which it has no deadline.

posts.title: Non-financial commercial real estate statistics
posts.label: 🧭 Negotiating mandate for trilogue talks
posts.summary: This proposal aims to establish a system for collecting and reporting statistics on non-financial commercial real estate properties. It seeks to provide standardized data on commercial property markets to help policymakers and analysts better understand economic trends in this sector.
posts.whatsNext: Trilogue talks with the Council can begin once the Council side has its own mandate. Closed-door rounds follow; timing is not published.

posts.title: Temporary trade-liberalisation measures applicable to Armenian products
posts.label: 🗳️ Parliament adopted its 1st-reading position
posts.summary: This proposal aims to temporarily reduce trade barriers on products from Armenia. The measure would seek to make it easier and cheaper to import Armenian goods into the EU market for a limited period.
posts.whatsNext: Council formal adoption is next, often without debate.

posts.title: Establishing the Union Customs Code and the European Union Customs Authority
posts.label: 🗳️ Parliament decided at 2nd reading
posts.summary: The proposal aims to create a new set of customs rules for trade across the EU and establish a dedicated authority to manage and enforce these customs procedures. This would streamline how goods are processed and taxed when moving between EU countries and their borders.
posts.whatsNext: If Parliament approved the Council position, the act is adopted and goes to signature. If amended, the Council has 3 months (+1 on request) to accept all amendments — otherwise conciliation. If rejected with absolute majority, the act falls.

posts.title: Sustainability-related disclosures in the financial services sector (SFDR) and key information documents for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (PRIIPs)
posts.label: 🗳️ Lead committee adopted its report
posts.summary: The proposal aims to require financial services companies to provide clearer information about how they consider environmental and social factors in their investments. It would also standardize the way investment products are explained to consumers so they can more easily compare different options.

posts.label: 📋 New legislative proposal
posts.summary: This proposal aims to simplify rules and reduce paperwork for the EU's outermost regions by modifying regulations that cover fishing, agriculture, trade, and related administrative requirements.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament gives a non-binding opinion, then the Council decides — usually by unanimity, with no deadline.

posts.title: Proposal for a DECISION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL renewing a Union action for the European Capitals of Culture for the years 2034 to 2047 and repealing Decision No 445/2014/EU
posts.label: 📋 New legislative proposal
posts.summary: This proposal aims to continue a cultural programme that designates certain European cities as Capitals of Culture for a future period. It would replace the current rules governing this initiative with updated provisions for the extended timeframe.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament's lead committee and the Council's working party examine it in parallel. No deadline applies at this stage; most files take one to two-plus years.

posts.title: Simplification of certain requirements for spatial information infrastructure in the Union (INSPIRE) (Omnibus VIII on environmental legislation)
posts.label: 🗳️ Lead committee adopted its report
posts.summary: This proposal aims to streamline and simplify the rules for how environmental and spatial information is collected, organized, and shared across the Union. It seeks to make it easier for authorities and organizations to handle geographic data while maintaining standards for environmental monitoring and reporting.
posts.whatsNext: A negotiating mandate for talks with the Council would usually follow, or the report goes straight to a plenary vote. No deadline applies.

posts.title: Empowering France to accede to the Inter-American Convention for the Protection and Conservation of Sea Turtles
posts.label: 🤝 Lead committee approved the trilogue deal
posts.summary: This proposal would allow France to join an international agreement focused on protecting and conserving sea turtles in the Americas. The measure aims to extend France's commitment to safeguarding these endangered marine animals through cooperation with other countries in the region.
posts.whatsNext: The deal is provisional: it still needs a plenary vote in Parliament and formal adoption by the Council. Although confirmation is expected, either institution can still decline.

posts.title: European Chemicals Agency and amending regulations
posts.label: 🤝 Lead committee approved the trilogue deal
posts.summary: This proposal would modify the rules governing the European Chemicals Agency and how it operates. It aims to update the regulations that establish and control this organization's responsibilities and procedures.
posts.whatsNext: The deal is provisional: it still needs a plenary vote in Parliament and formal adoption by the Council. Although confirmation is expected, either institution can still decline.

posts.title: Establishing the Union Customs Code and the European Union Customs Authority
posts.label: 🧭 Council adopted its 1st-reading position
posts.summary: The proposal aims to create a new set of customs rules for trade across the EU and establish a dedicated authority to manage and enforce these customs procedures. This would streamline how goods are processed and taxed when moving between EU countries and their borders.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament's 2nd reading: 3 months (+1 on request) to approve the text (the act is then adopted), amend it, or reject it — amendment or rejection needs an absolute majority of all MEPs (361 of 720). Approval is likely here: the position reflects a negotiated deal.

posts.title: Proposal for a REGULATION OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL establishing a framework of measures for strengthening the Union innovation ecosystem and amending Regulation (EU) 2017/1001 (European Innovation Act)
posts.label: 📋 New legislative proposal
posts.summary: This proposal aims to strengthen Europe's ability to innovate by establishing a framework of supporting measures across the continent. It would also make changes to existing rules governing European trademarks and designs.
posts.whatsNext: Parliament's lead committee and the Council's working party examine it in parallel. No deadline applies at this stage; most files take one to two-plus years.
